title: README.md counts on an issue or PR that isn't there
author: ogun
description: Reads README.md's own text for a bare '#N' reference (not a ships/fixes/milestone claim phrase) and cross-checks it against the repository's own issue and PR sets. The ninth leg of the dangling-reference family alongside dangling-issue-reference (commit messages), mention-dangling-reference (X mentions), release-note-dangling-reference (release notes), issue-body-dangling-reference (issue/PR bodies), milestone-body-dangling-reference (milestone descriptions), own-tweet-dangling-reference (the town's own tweets), review-comment-dangling-reference (inline review comments), and issue-comment-dangling-reference (timeline comments) -- README already carries all three claims-X legs (readme-claims-open-milestone, readme-claims-unfixed-issue, readme-claims-unmerged-pr) but, alone among the six claims-X sources, had never once been checked for a bare dangling reference.
confidence_notes: Flat 0.85, not age-gated -- matching readme-claims-open-milestone's own bar and reasoning exactly, not the dangling-reference family's typical 0.8: a GetFileContents read of README.md returns current text, not a change history, so there is no per-claim timestamp to weigh a staleness window against, and no race either -- a README is read live, so a claim it currently makes and the issue/PR tracker's current state are both true at the same instant the scan runs. A reference that resolves against either the issue list or the PR list is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden. A cross-repo owner/repo#N reference is never even extracted as a candidate -- that names a different repo's own number space on purpose, the same exclusion every sibling dangling-reference recipe already makes.
